# Fixture: Discussion Wishlist

## Flawed manuscript input

The proposed system opens a promising direction for general robotic
manipulation. Because it combines active perception and guarded execution, it
can be extended to many contact-rich tasks, including cable routing, assembly,
and deformable-object manipulation. Future work will apply the framework to
more objects, more robots, and more industrial scenarios. The current results
also suggest that active observation is a general solution to visual occlusion
in manipulation.

The paragraph is not grounded in the actual evidence. It turns one insertion
setting into a broad program, and it treats future work as if it were already
supported. It does not name the current limitation precisely. It does not say
which assumption may fail under new fixtures, cameras, robot arms, or object
types. A top-tier Discussion should interpret what the present evidence means,
then draw a boundary that motivates a testable next step.

## Expected audit pressure

The skill should replace broad future claims with limitation-derived future
work. It should state what was actually tested, what remains untested, and what
new evidence would be required for the broader claim.

## Failure modes

- Wish-list future work.
- Broad implication without boundary.
- AI-like promising-direction language.
- General solution claim without cross-task evidence.
